expectations.text: Recommends ACBC for this specific case (9 attributes + complex pricing)
expectations.evidence: 'ACBC is the right call for 9 attributes. The complexity is real but proportionate — you would have non-attendance problems in standard CBC at this attribute count.' Decision table also shows ACBC as primary recommendation for 9-attribute + summed pricing.

expectations.text: Mentions at least one ACBC failure mode (BYO seeding bias, unacceptable inflation, or simulator limitations)
expectations.evidence: All three mentioned: 'BYO seeding bias — respondents anchor on what they built in BYO. Importance scores from ACBC are typically more spread.' 'Unacceptable inflation risk — if more than ~10-15% of respondents have a possibility set smaller than 8, you have a problem.' 'Simulator coverage outside the consideration set — ACBC simulators are most reliable for products in or near the consideration zone.'

expectations.text: Notes that ACBC is NOT the default for simpler studies
expectations.evidence: Decision table entry: 'Survey length is a hard constraint -> CBC with partial-profile (not ACBC).' Also: 'Don't over-index on importance scores from ACBC' and explicit list of conditions where CBC is preferred.

eval_feedback.overall: All assertions pass. Notably, the skill added a Menu-Based Conjoint recommendation for add-on pricing, which is beyond the base assertions and represents genuine expert-level disambiguation.
